items.english: If the roots of the two squares whose sum equals the prime 4n+1 differ by one, so that 4n+1 = p² + (p−1)², then, since q = p−1, the following operation will be obtained.
whence a = 1·p + 1·(p−1) = 2p−1, and in general a = (4n+1)m ± (2p−1).

items.english: If all squares are sought which, increased by one, are divisible by the prime number 2 = 1+1
